technical_requirements_summary: Primary workload: conversational chat (short completions) plus night-time reranking jobs; target p95 <= 200ms for <512 token completions, p99 <= 500ms for larger reranks. Steady-state baseline ~250 QPS, avg 40 tokens/request (~10k tokens/sec steady). Peak transient target 600 QPS for marketing bursts (~24k tokens/sec). Want reserved GPU pool sized to keep p95 SLA under 200ms for steady-state; burst autoscaling or pre-allocated burst capacity to handle peaks. Prefer H100-class GPUs; will accept quantized A100 variants if cost benefit is clear. KV cache warm-up time must be considered for cold-start windows.
workshop_goals: Establish baseline QPS and tokens/sec from sampled traces
Define steady-state capacity required to meet p95 latency SLO
Quantify burst headroom vs reserved capacity trade-offs
Produce recommended reserved GPU counts + instance types
Agree on SLA terms: throughput guarantees, latency SLOs, crediting model
benchmark_inputs_requested: 30-day anonymized traffic sample (JSON lines) - include timestamps and token counts
Representative heavy rerank queries and batch sizes
Desired p95/p99 latency targets and cost per token expectations
poC_plan: 2-week POC: deploy a dedicated pool (3-5 GPUs) + replay 2 peak windows; measure tokens/sec, p95/p99, GPU utilization, model switch fallbacks. Deliverables: POC report with bottlenecks + recommended reserve counts and pricing options.
pricing_notes: Customer prefers committed monthly pricing with predictable unit rates; exploring 12-month reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go bursts. Finance asked for a model showing unit cost at 8/16/32 reserved GPUs.
